description: Ambrosia is a Linux distro on Arch that looks and moves as one thing: one design authority, one token file, a generator theming every toolkit identically. It ships as Arch packages and an archiso installer image. The design system, preview and review site exist; the distro pipeline (packages, Ambrosia session on KWin, live image, installer) has a first cut; the shell has its menu bar and traffic-light window frames.
features: Single OKLCH token file generates GTK, KDE, KWin frame, QML, web, JSON; gamut-mapped to sRGB
Derives contrast-checked accent variants from the token file
Solves response/damping springs into constants and easing curves
Validates contrast, concentric radii, and spacing grid via tests
Browser mock desktop preview and review site render spec with live specimens
Dark mode and accents via keys/URL; verdict threads in review
Installs themes per-user on Linux preserving prior configs
Mac-first keyboard: Super-as-Command, ⌘ glyphs in menus, Files shortcuts
Signed Arch pacman repo on GitHub; archiso installer, UEFI, QEMU-testable
Menu bar: focused-app menus with shortcuts, Wi-Fi, search, clock
Super+Space Spotlight: apps, file results, Settings panes, sums; dock keeps pinned order, separate launchers, Mac-style Trash
Control center: pure blur glass, modes, notification banners with actions
Honey-bowl Ambrosia branding in menu bar, banner, favicon, preview and review site
Finder-style Files: thumbnails, Quick Look, Get Info, Columns with metadata, undo, search, drives with eject, Show in Folder
Colour tags shared with Dolphin/Baloo: dots, tinted folders, menu, sidebar lists

Settings: Wi‑Fi, Network/VPN, Bluetooth, Sound, Displays, Battery, Privacy, Users, Lock Screen, Wallpaper, Updates, Storage, Clock, Language, Sharing, Login Items, Printers & Scanners, Accessibility, Spotlight

preview.summary: Preview Desktop is a static HTML/JS mock macOS-like desktop for visually reviewing generated tokens. It renders draggable/focusable windows, menubar popups, sliders, control center, dock, and a live clock with no build step beyond `make build`. Every color, type, radius, shadow, and motion value comes from dist/web/tokens.css; preview.css holds only mock-desktop layout positions, and the menubar/README/favicon use the Ambrosia bowl logo while assets/ also holds the hand-drawn Files app icon.

map.name: Mock desktop shell (wallpaper, menubar, dock, windows)
Control center (capsule modules, toggles, sliders, Edit Controls)
Dock (padding, glassy icons, tooltip, badges, separators)
Glass material recipe
Theme and accent switching (D / A keys, URL params)
Draggable and focusable windows
Menubar popups / menus
Live clock
App-icon squircle mask
Ambrosia bowl branding (menubar logo, favicon)
Files app icon (Finder-style two-tone face, Dock Files pin)

flows.name: View updated tokens
steps: Run make build to regenerate dist/web/tokens.css
Open preview/index.html which links tokens.css + glass.css + preview.css
preview.js reads ?theme= / ?accent= params and prefers-color-scheme
Toggle with D (dark mode) and A (accent cycle) to review

flows.name: Window interaction
steps: Click window to focus (preview.js manages z-order / active class)
Drag via titlebar to reposition (layout literals in preview.css)
Open menubar popups / sliders to check glass and controls

files: preview/index.html — mock desktop markup, SVG icon sprite, stylesheet links (requires dist/web/tokens.css)
preview/preview.js — theme/accent switching, popups, draggable windows, sliders, clock, squircle mask
preview/preview.css — mock-desktop layout; all design values via var(--amb-*) / var(--glass-*)
preview/glass.css — shared glass recipe (tint, blur, rim, edge, specular ring, grain)
assets/ambrosia.svg — bowl-with-scoops-and-spoon brand mark used in menubar and preview
assets/icon.svg — app/favicon form of the bowl mark
assets/icons/org.ambrosia.files.svg — hand-drawn Files app icon on a blue squircle, matched to the macOS Dock grid
rules: Never hardcode design values in preview/*.css — use vars from dist/web/tokens.css; only layout positions may be literals.
Run `make build` first — preview is broken/stale without generated dist/web/tokens.css.
Do not add build tooling or JS dependencies — static HTML/JS only.
Keep glass.css shared-safe — it is also used by the review site, so no preview-specific layout in it.
Round inner panels (e.g. sidebar) to their own outer corners — scaled-down blur is cut to the window shape only if the panel itself is rounded, otherwise corners render sharp/square.
Keep file selection highlight behind the icon — replacing the document page fill with selection color turns clicked icons black.
Draw app icons by hand as our own vectors; never trace Apple's artwork, and keep reference screenshots of macOS only in the gitignored out/ folder.
edges: Design Tokens via dist/web/tokens.css — sole source of colors, type, radii, shadows, springs; preview breaks without a build
Build and Install — `make build` generates dist/web/tokens.css that preview links
Shell Dock and Packaging — the Files icon in assets/icons/org.ambrosia.files.svg is the Dock's Files pin and is installed by the package build

design-tokens.summary: Single-file source of truth for ambrosia's look and motion, exporting type scale, 4px spacing, radii, OKLCH colors, glass/materials, shadows, springs, and window-frame metrics. All dist themes are generated from it via tools/gen, so this file is edited instead of generated output. Newcomer must grasp: colors are OKLCH strings for perceptually even lightness and everything is light/dark Mode pairs.

map.name: Type scale and fonts
Spacing grid (4px)
Radii and icon corners
Light/dark color pairs
Palette and accents
Status and window-control colors (traffic lights)
Window frame metrics (titlebar, traffic lights)
Glass and materials
Shadows
Springs and motion
Control center module metrics
Dock metrics
The pointer's shapes (arrow, hands, I-beam, resize arrows, badges, the busy wheel), hotspots and other names
App icons for the stand-in apps (Terminal, text editor, viewers, Calculator, archiver, store, Screenshot, system info) and the icon names they answer to
Controls other Qt apps get (push, field, check, slider, menu, tab, box, row sizes; controlColor)

files: design/tokens.ts — the single source of truth: font/type/tracking, space, radius, OKLCH color pairs, window frame, glass, shadow, springs
design/DESIGN.md — reasoning behind the numbers before retuning values
design/DECISIONS.md — recorded design decisions behind token choices
design/cursors.ts — every pointer shape as paths on a 32-unit canvas (nominal size 24), in groups painted rim-then-ink; pointers(colors) takes the token colors it borrows from the generator
design/icons.ts — app icons as SVG art on a 256 grid (tile 24..232, gradient pair, names); adopted maps Files' and Settings' existing icons to KDE's names
rules: Never hand-edit generated output in dist/; change design/tokens.ts and regenerate.
Keep colors as OKLCH strings (oklch(L C H) or with / A) so generator can convert and gamut-map to sRGB.
Provide both light and dark values via Mode/Pair for mode-dependent tokens.
See DESIGN.md for reasoning behind the numbers before retuning values.
Window-control colours (traffic lights, light and dark) are measured from macOS 26; light-mode traffic-light colours match the dark-mode ones on the Mac.
Traffic-light edges are a thin darker shade of each light's own colour, not grey.
Menus snap open instantly with no open animation (close fades 120ms); control-center panel is blur-only with no fill, border, or shadow, controls carry their own glass.

font.ui lists Inter Variable before the static Inter: Qt maps Inter.ttc (13 MB, every cut) once per weight. Weight 700 then needs QT_NO_SYNTHESIZED_BOLD (session font environment), or Qt fakes bold over the variable font's real Bold.
Pointer shapes are drawn by hand in design/cursors.ts: never extract or trace Apple's cursor images, even though the look (black ink, white rim, soft shadow) follows a Mac's.
edges: Generator Core — resolves design/tokens.ts: OKLCH to sRGB, contrast, springs, dist orchestration
Theme Targets — format the resolved model into GTK, KDE, QML, fontconfig, web output; kdecoration target carries window-frame metrics and lights to the KWin decoration plugin
Preview Desktop — styled only from generated dist/web/tokens.css, never this file directly

review-site.summary: The Review Site is a design-review web app that renders every `## ` section of DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md as a reviewable item with live specimens, a verdict and a notes thread. Specimens are built with the same tokens and resolver the generator ships, so review matches output. State lives in `design/review.json` via a Bun server when present, otherwise in browser localStorage; `build.ts` emits a static fallback into `dist/site/`.

map.name: Live specimens per spec section
Review page layout and sections
Verdict buttons and notes thread
Review state, server/local fallback
Review server and persistence API
Review items sourced from design docs
Theme / accent appearance switcher
Site styling in own design language
Static site build
Icon sprite reuse from preview
Element builder helper

flows.name: Review a design item
steps: content.ts splits DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md into items
main.ts renders section with reasoning plus specimens
review.ts load() tries /api/review, falls back to localStorage
user sets verdict / posts note via setVerdict/addMessage
server.ts queues write into design/review.json or local mode saves locally
onChange listeners re-render verdict and thread

flows.name: Serve live review
steps: server.ts serves index.html with HMR on port 4747
STATIC preview/, dist/web/, assets/ served as plain files
client fetches /api/review for shared state
POST verdict/message serialized through one write queue

flows.name: Build static review site
steps: build.ts Bun.builds index.html into dist/site/
copies preview, dist/web, assets/wallpapers alongside
no server: review.ts stays in localStorage mode

files: site/main.ts — page assembly, appearance switcher, verdict/thread UI wiring
site/specimens.ts — live token/resolver-driven examples per spec section
site/review.ts — verdict/thread state with server-then-localStorage fallback
site/server.ts — Bun server, hot reload, queued writes to design/review.json
site/content.ts — parses DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md headings into review items
site/site.css — review-site styling; values only from dist/web/tokens.css
site/build.ts — static build into dist/site/ plus preview asset copies
site/index.html — shell: sidebar, toolbar, content, wallpaper, sprite mounts

rules: Never hardcode review copy: items and intros come from DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md via content.ts.
No ad-hoc styling values: every value comes from dist/web/tokens.css, glass from preview/glass.css.
Verdicts are only approve/change/discuss (or null); server rejects anything else.
Review writes must go through the single queued writer; concurrent writes interleave otherwise.
Do not assume the server exists: static builds must keep verdicts/notes in localStorage.
Static build must copy preview, dist/web, assets/wallpapers or the preview iframe breaks.

Generator Core — specimens render through tools/gen resolve, color, spring
Preview Desktop — embeds preview/index.html in iframe; reuses its icon sprite and preview/glass.css
Build and Install — static output lands in dist/site/; live site consumes dist/web/tokens.css
Theme Targets — specimens show what formatters will ship; review approves that output

build-install.summary: This layer builds, tests and installs Ambrosia. Bun and TypeScript handle the build, Make orchestrates the targets, and a POSIX sh script installs the already-generated themes for the current Linux user into XDG config and data directories. Install copies from dist/ and backs up foreign files. The key idea: install never loses user data, since foreign files become <name>.before-ambrosia and ambrosia-owned files are overwritten silently. Make publish also pushes the signed Arch package repo to GitHub Releases.

map.name: Per-user theme install
GTK variant selection (light/dark via gsettings)
Backup of pre-existing user files
make package / quickshell / iso targets (Arch)
Publish signed Arch package repo (make publish)
Running the build gate, review site and screenshots on tenet (make remote-build, review-remote, shot-remote)
Drawing pieces of the shell with no window (make shell-shots)

flows.name: Install themes
steps: Resolve dist/ relative to script location
Exit early (success) on non-Linux, pointing at dist/
Detect GTK mode via gsettings color-scheme (default light)
place() each dist artifact into XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME, backing up foreign files

flows.name: Publish package repo
steps: make publish runs tools/publish-repo.sh
Build the packages under packaging/
Sign the repo db with the private key, which stays on the Mac
Copy ambrosia.db and ambrosia.files as real files, since release assets cannot be symlinks
Upload to the rolling `repo` release in justin06lee/ambrosia-packages

flows.name: Remote work
steps: make remote-build / review-remote / shot-remote (Mac)
tools/remote.sh pushes HEAD to tenet's bare repo ~/git/ambrosia.git
~/work/ambrosia resets to it, uncommitted changes rsynced on top
the command runs capped there
review-remote tunnels localhost:4747 over ssh; shot-remote (headless Firefox, 1440x900) copies out/shots/<SHOT>.png back

files: tools/install.sh — installs dist/ themes per-user with .before-ambrosia backups and GTK light/dark pick
Makefile — build, test, dist, package and publish targets, and the remote-* / shot-remote targets that run on tenet
tools/publish-repo.sh — builds, signs and uploads the pacman repo to the public releases
rules: Run from any cwd: dist path is derived from the script location, not cwd.
Non-Linux is not an error: exit 0 after pointing at dist/.
Only files lacking the 'Generated by ambrosia' marker are backed up; never delete a .before-ambrosia backup by overwriting blindly.
GTK3 gets only the active mode file copied as gtk.css; GTK cannot follow system scheme alone.
The private signing key never goes into either repo; it lives only on the Mac.
The source repo stays private; the public ambrosia-packages repo carries built shell QML and session scripts.
Release assets cannot be symlinks, so the publish step must upload real copies of ambrosia.db and ambrosia.files.
After Arch updates Qt, bump pkgrel in packaging/quickshell/PKGBUILD and run make publish.

Heavy work runs on tenet, not the 8 GB Mac: the Mac only edits, runs git and signs. Everything on tenet runs capped (systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=…, nice 19, ionice -c3, two jobs): it has no swap and hosts mira's gateway.

make shot-remote shows layout and colour, not glass: headless Firefox draws no backdrop blur.
tools/qmlshot can load only QML that needs nothing but Qt Quick and the Theme: keep a new shell surface's picture in its own file, apart from its Quickshell window, and add a sheet for it.

Linux desktop (XDG dirs, gsettings) — reads color-scheme, writes into XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME

GitHub Releases — make publish uploads the repo to the rolling `repo` release in justin06lee/ambrosia-packages

theme-targets.summary: This layer turns the resolved theme model (Resolved/ResolvedMode from Generator Core) into per-toolkit output files. Each file in tools/gen/targets/ is a pure formatter: roles/colors plus shared helpers. Newcomers must grasp that nothing is resolved here; token truth and color math live upstream, and targets only map and serialize.

map.name: GTK theme overrides
Traffic lights (window buttons) across KWin, GTK and QML
KDE color schemes
QML singleton for shell
Web CSS custom properties
Fontconfig aliases and rasterization
Shared formatting helpers
Session kdeglobals (light scheme + type-scale fonts as QFont strings)
KWin window frame's tokens (titlebar, lights, corner, rim, edge, shadow) as a C++ header for decoration/
Pointer theme (Xcursor files, KWin's cursors_scalable SVGs, web/cursors.css, the look-over sheet)
Icon theme (index.theme, apps/scalable, alias links, web/icons.css, the icon sheet)

flows.name: Resolved model to toolkit file
steps: Generator Core produces Resolved / ResolvedMode
Target maps roles to toolkit vocabulary (libadwaita vars, KDE sets, QML tree, CSS vars)
Colors serialized via color helpers (toCss, toKde, toQtHex) and shared helpers (HEADER, pt, fontStack, kebab/slug)
Formatter returns file string for dist orchestration to write

files: tools/gen/targets/shared.ts — shared header, kebab/slug, fontStack, cssShadow, pt helpers, and the window-button symbol shapes
tools/gen/targets/gtk.ts — libadwaita CSS vars (gtk4), named colors per mode (gtk3), and GTK's traffic-light sizing and edge
tools/gen/targets/kde.ts — opaque .colors sets, translucency flattened onto background
tools/gen/targets/qml.ts — Ambrosia QML singleton tree with Theme.dark / Theme.accentName switching, and Theme.tileIcons (the icon theme's tile names, for the Dock)
tools/gen/targets/web.ts — --amb-* CSS custom properties for preview/web surfaces
tools/gen/targets/fontconfig.ts — sans-serif/monospace aliases, rasterization defaults, and the session's font environment (FreeType stem darkening, QT_NO_SYNTHESIZED_BOLD)
tools/gen/targets/kdecoration.ts — dist/kdecoration/tokens.h: the frame's sizes, per-mode colors, window-button shapes, light edge and shadow layers for the decoration plugin

tools/gen/targets/cursors.ts — the pointer inside dist/icons/Ambrosia (cursors/ Xcursor files, cursors_scalable/ SVGs with metadata.json), dist/web/cursors.css (--amb-cursor-* and --amb-pointer-*), dist/cursors/sheet.html; rasterizes with @resvg/resvg-js

tools/gen/targets/icons.ts — dist/icons/Ambrosia: index.theme (Inherits breeze,breeze_cursors,hicolor; FollowsColorScheme), apps/scalable/*.svg, links for other names; tileIconNames() feeds Theme.tileIcons; dist/icons/sheet.html, dist/web/icons.css
tools/gen/targets/qstyle.ts — dist/qstyle/tokens.h for style/: the controls' sizes, controlColor per mode, and each mode's palette for the gallery
rules: Do not edit generated output; every file carries HEADER pointing back to design/tokens.ts via tools/gen.
Do not resolve or derive colors here; use the passed Resolved model and color.ts / resolve.ts helpers.
KDE output must stay opaque r,g,b: flatten translucent values with flat() onto their background set.
GTK3 has no prefers-color-scheme: emit one file per mode; GTK4 emits light and dark in one file.
Keep QML identifiers safe: slug token keys and prefix leading digits.
QML property names can't be ECMAScript keywords; qml.ts suffixes them with _ (Theme.size.switch_), guarded by a test in tools/gen/rules.test.ts.
Window-control colors are per mode (resolved modes[m].windowControls, with inactive = fill.primary on the window); QML exposes them as Theme.windowControls, which follows Theme.dark.
Window-button symbol shapes (×, −, zoom) are defined once in shared.ts; KWin, GTK and QML draw from that definition, so change them there, not per toolkit.
Traffic lights must measure the same in every toolkit: 14 pt wide, 23 pt apart, symbols 50% black; a change to one toolkit's sizing needs the others checked against it.
Traffic-light colours are the same in light and dark mode, as on macOS; do not give light mode its own set.
The traffic-light edge is a thin darker shade of each light's own colour, not a grey ring; the KWin frame and GTK draw it that way.
GTK lights move to the left only in sessions started after that setting shipped; a running session keeps the old placement, so check on a fresh login.

Qt fakes bold for weight ≥700 when the face's OS/2 weight class is under 700. Variable fonts report their default instance (Inter Variable says 400), so their real Bold gets thickened again. fontEnvironment() sets QT_NO_SYNTHESIZED_BOLD=1, which startambrosia sources at login. fontconfig's embolden doesn't reach Qt.

The pointer's shadow is blurred once by resvg and embedded in each cursors_scalable SVG as a PNG <image>, so it looks the same in any renderer (Breeze's own SVGs use feGaussianBlur, which KWin's QSvgRenderer does draw); only the web variant uses a filter. A test keeps <filter> out of the theme's SVGs.
resvg-js returns premultiplied RGBA, which is what Xcursor wants: don't premultiply again. Pass font.loadSystemFonts false or every render scans the system's fonts.

rules: Build file URLs from Quickshell.shellDir with an explicit file:// — Quickshell's QML base URL is qrc:/qs-blackhole, so relative URLs and Qt.resolvedUrl don't reach files.
All values come from import Ambrosia (Theme.*); never hard-code colors or sizes that a token has.
Dock and Trash artwork is hand-drawn vector art; never copy or extract Apple's images from Dock.app or any system bundle.

The Dock's Trash is sized against its neighbouring icons by macOS's squircle-to-bin ratio; resize it with them, not on its own.
Window traffic lights use macOS's colours in both light and dark mode, and each light's edge is a thin darker shade of its own colour, not grey.

KWin gives its window list (org_kde_plasma_window_management) only to programs a desktop file grants, matched by Exec path: org.ambrosia.shell.desktop names /usr/bin/quickshell. No other desktop file may Exec /usr/bin/quickshell (KWin takes the first match), so shortcuts run /usr/bin/ambrosia.

Plasma's appmenu kded only collects apps' menus while org.kde.kappmenuview is on the bus; Apps.qml holds it with dbus-test-tool black-hole. Apps check at startup, so ones started before the shell keep their in-window menus.
A QML file loaded by file:// URL (Loader) gets its own copies of the shell's singletons; pass it values instead (AppMenu.qml).

Menus, the control center and confirmations draw on Overlay.qml, a grabbing PopupWindow of the menu bar: KWin sends it keys without activating it, so the app stays active (Search, a keyboard-taking layer surface, deactivates it). It spans the screen, bar strip masked: Qt hands an open popup the bar's pointer events by position. Apps.frozen holds the bar's app; window actions capture their window at open.
Compare a window with the screen it was made for (home), not its live screen, which changes as it maps and unmaps and loops through visible.
Start apps through kstart (Session.launch/run), never execDetached on the app: it would live in ambrosia-shell.service's cgroup and die when the shell restarts.
Pinned apps' AppId ends in .desktop, running ones' not (use Apps.entryFor). Windows keep their pin's Dock spot only with launchInPlace and separateLaunchers: true.

Quickshell links Qt internals: when Arch updates qt6-base, bump pkgrel in packaging/quickshell/PKGBUILD and make publish (it rebuilds Quickshell when the release lacks that version).
Any change to dbusmenu-source.patch must update its checksum and bump pkgrel in packaging/quickshell/PKGBUILD, because make publish only rebuilds Quickshell for a version the release lacks.

The patch must make Quickshell send DBusMenu AboutToShow on every menu open, not only the first: Qt raises a menu's aboutToShow only from that call, so apps tracking open menus miss every later open otherwise.
packaging/PKGBUILD must install ambrosia-shell's pacman restart hook (session/ambrosia-shell-restart.hook); without it, upgraded shell QML waits for the next login to take effect.
Installing an ambrosia-shell package with pacman restarts the shell at once, which cuts into any demo or recording running on the desktop.

Installing ambrosia-desktop on tenet needs a full system upgrade (pacman -Syu) first: its new depends would pull packages from a list newer than tenet's system and partially upgrade it (Avahi, for one).
tools/remote.sh must build only in its own checkout on tenet: a build run in another lane's checkout ships that lane's code, and a harmless rsync error must not stop the build.

generator-core.summary: Generator Core resolves design/tokens.ts into a concrete sRGB + solved-spring model that every target formats. It is built as Bun+TypeScript: color math, spring solver, a per-mode resolver, and a dist orchestrator. A newcomer must grasp that targets never read tokens directly; resolve() is the single agreement point for derived colors and motion.

map.name: Token resolution (per-mode model)
OKLCH to sRGB conversion with gamut mapping
Contrast derivation and label flattening
Accent derivation (bg/fg/text/hover/pressed/highlight)
Spring solving (response/damping to constants/curve)
Dist orchestration (generate all targets)
Window frame target (KWin decoration traffic lights)

flows.name: Generate dist from tokens
steps: tools/gen/index.ts calls resolve()
resolve.ts parses OKLCH via color.ts and solves springs via spring.ts
index.ts passes Resolved model to each formatter in tools/gen/targets/ (including kdecoration.ts)
Formatted strings written to dist/ paths (web, gtk, kde, qml, fontconfig, kdecoration) plus resolved dump

flows.name: Derive a concrete color
steps: parseOklch() parses oklch() string
toLinear + gamut-mapped conversion to RGBA in color.ts
over()/withAlpha() composite translucency
contrast()/ensureContrast() enforce readability for accents and labels

files: tools/gen/resolve.ts — resolves tokens.ts into per-mode Resolved colors, accents, material, glass, shadows and springs
tools/gen/index.ts — orchestrates generation: resolves once, formats every target, writes dist/
tools/gen/color.ts — OKLCH parsing, OKLCH to sRGB with gamut mapping, compositing, contrast, and output formatters
tools/gen/spring.ts — solves (response, damping) springs into stiffness/damping, settle duration, and sampled curve

tools/gen/xcursor.ts — writes (and, for tests, reads) Xcursor files: every size and frame of one pointer shape, premultiplied RGBA in
rules: Never read design/tokens.ts directly from a target for colors — go through resolve() so derived accents and flattened labels agree everywhere.
Never bypass color.ts gamut mapping and contrast helpers with ad-hoc conversion — out-of-gamut OKLCH and unreadable text result.
Keep Resolved/ResolvedMode/ResolvedAccent shapes stable — every formatter in tools/gen/targets/ depends on them.
index.ts writes text or bytes, then the icon theme's alias symlinks (other names for an icon or a pointer shape).
index.ts reads assets/icons/<name>.svg for the icons the theme adopts and hands them to iconTheme(); the theme lives at dist/icons/Ambrosia (not dist/cursors/Ambrosia) and must be copied with cp -a.

Theme Targets — sole consumer: every formatter takes the Resolved model from resolve(); kdecoration.ts builds the window frame from it
Build and Install — runs the generator to produce dist/ before install and test

settings/qml/SoftwareUpdatePage.qml — the Software Update pane and its Update Now confirm sheet
settings/qml/PrivacyAppsPage.qml — the per-permission sub-page listing the apps
settings/src/about.h — declarations behind the About pane's system data
settings/src/connectiondetails.cpp — saved connection settings read and applied for the Details… sheets
rules: No dead rows: a pane is listed only if it has a page here or an installed KDE module; Apple-only items (serial number, AppleCare, legal lines, startup chime, interface sound effects) are left out, not faked
Privileged changes go through each service's own polkit (hostnamed, timedated, NetworkManager…), never a root helper of ours
Zoom is vertical only, like System Settings: App::zoom runs a KWin script (setMaximize(v, false)); xdg-shell's maximize would fill the screen's width
Pane tests on tenet must never switch off Wi‑Fi, its only network connection; put back any audio or network value a test changed
Pane tests on tenet must remove any test VPN profile afterwards, since the VPN page switches a real WireGuard profile and could take the default route
Date & Time and Language & Region tests change the clock and system locale, so they run only in the VM; on the real system the clock, timezone, NTP and locale stay untouched
Update Now asks for an administrator's password: our polkit rule (packaging/polkit/10-ambrosia-packagekit.rules) sorts ahead of Arch's, which let wheel update with none
pulseaudio-qt has no level monitor, so the input meter opens its own peak-detect stream in sound.cpp

Clicks act through MouseArea, not TapHandler: Qt 6 hands a press an item above took to the handlers of every item beneath, so a TapHandler under a menu or sheet fires too. Only the window's background, lights and toolbar keep TapHandlers; menus are modal
Sheets stack (SettingsWindow.sheets): only the top one takes keys and clicks; one under another draws inactive
Battery/Energy are tested in the VM against scratch/settings/fake-upower.py, Trackpad against fake-touchpad.py (a uinput clickpad), never tenet's own
edges: theme-targets — import Ambrosia (dist/qml Theme) for type and glyphs
shell-and-session — MenuBar, ControlCenter and the Dock pin open it through Session.settings(pane)
packaging-and-image — ambrosia-settings split package in packaging/PKGBUILD; ambrosia-desktop depends on it
